name: Hydrafacial Keravive

card.summary: Salon scalp facial from HydraFacial pitched for scalp health and hair quality; only registered studies, no published results.
card.note: Registered studies have no published results.

quick.overview:
Keravive is a clinic scalp treatment that cleanses, exfoliates and applies serums to the scalp. It is marketed for scalp health and hair quality, including for thinning hair.

Two small studies are registered, one completed in androgenetic alopecia, but no results were found.
quick.mechanism: A handheld device performs cleansing and exfoliation and delivers topical products to the scalp, in the manner of the brand's facial treatment.
quick.risks: No safety data were found in the sources reviewed. Whether it affects hair growth has not been shown by published trials.

lead: Hydrafacial Keravive, also marketed as HydraScalp, is a salon and clinic scalp treatment from the Hydrafacial brand that adapts its multi-step facial platform to the scalp. It cleanses and exfoliates the scalp, applies peptide-containing serums and is marketed to people with thinning hair or a dry, itchy, congested scalp, with the goal of a healthier scalp and hair that looks fuller and shinier. [1][3]

The company describes three steps: purify (light suction and exfoliation to open the follicles), nourish (peptides and hydration applied to the cleansed follicles) and boost (a daily take-home peptide spray). [3] It recommends a series, usually three treatments about a month apart, with each session taking roughly 30 to 60 minutes depending on whether the whole scalp is treated. [3]

Hydrafacial states the treatment is clinically proven to help reduce hair thinning, citing a pilot study run by the company, in which 75% of participants reported improved hair fullness after one treatment and 82% reported shinier, healthier-looking hair by the third visit. [3] Independent published results are not yet available; two studies are registered, one completed in androgenetic alopecia. [1][2]

chain: Suction and exfoliation clear the scalp and follicle openings
Peptide and hydration serums are applied to the follicles
Healthier scalp and hair that looks fuller and shinier
angle.text: People book Keravive sessions to improve scalp condition and the appearance of thin or dull hair, usually as a series of monthly visits with a take-home spray. Fuller-looking hair and a calmer scalp are the outcomes the brand describes. [3]

infobox: Scalp cleansing and exfoliation with serum delivery
Three treatments about a month apart, plus daily spray [3]
Niacinamide, a Keravive peptide complex, vitamin B5 with arginine [3]

paras: The treatment applies Hydrafacial's approach of cleansing, exfoliating and infusing products, here to the scalp. [3] Per the company, it is marketed to men and women with hair loss, thinning or poor scalp health, and is described as suitable for all scalp and hair types, including braids, extensions, locks and dyed hair. Providers may recommend it alongside other hair restoration or scalp treatments. [3]

Hydrafacial reports that after three monthly treatments plus daily spray use, users described a smoother scalp with less itching, reduced hair loss and thinning, and hair that looks and feels thicker. [3] The company notes that the cited results come from company-sponsored studies and testimonials, and that individual results vary. [3]

NCT06112782, "Keravive by Hydrafacial for Scalp Health and Enhanced Hair Quality," enrolled 44 participants with androgenetic alopecia, began in July 2019 and is listed as completed; no peer-reviewed results were located. [2]
NCT07935993 is planned to begin in November 2026 with 15 participants with self-perceived hair thinning, testing a scalp serum paired with the HydraScalp Keravive treatment. [1]

timeline.event: A study of Keravive for scalp health and hair quality in androgenetic alopecia starts. [2]
A trial pairing a scalp serum with the treatment is registered for people with hair thinning. [1]
